title: Quantifying Memorization and Privacy Risks in Genomic Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.08913v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Genomic language models (GLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for learning representations of DNA sequences, enabling advances in variant prediction, regulatory element identification, and cross-task transfer learning. However, as these models are increasingly trained or fine-tuned on sensitive genomic cohorts, they risk memorizing specific sequences from their training data, raising serious concerns around privacy, data leakage, and regulatory compliance. Despite growing awareness of memorization risks in general-purpose language models, little systematic evaluation exists for these risks in the genomic domain, where data exhibit unique properties such as a fixed nucleotide alphabet, strong biological structure, and individual identifiability. We present a comprehensive, multi-vector privacy evaluation framework designed to quantify memorization risks in GLMs. Our approach integrates three complementary risk assessment methodologies

translated_title: 基因组语言模型中的记忆化与隐私风险量化研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：基因组语言模型（GLMs）已成为学习DNA序列表示的有力工具，推动了变异预测、调控元件识别和跨任务迁移学习等领域的进展。然而，随着这些模型越来越多地在敏感基因组队列上进行训练或微调，它们存在记忆训练数据中特定序列的风险，引发了关于隐私、数据泄露和监管合规的严重担忧。尽管人们越来越意识到通用语言模型中的记忆化风险，但在基因组领域，对这些风险的系统性评估仍然很少，而该领域的数据具有独特的性质，如固定的核苷酸字母表、强烈的生物结构和个体可识别性。我们提出了一个全面的、多向量的隐私评估框架，旨在量化GLMs中的记忆化风险。我们的方法整合了三种互补的风险评估方法。
tldr: 本文提出了首个针对基因组语言模型的系统性多向量隐私评估框架，通过整合三种互补方法量化其记忆化风险，填补了该领域隐私评估的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic multi-vector privacy evaluation framework for genomic language models, quantifying memorization risks by integrating three complementary assessment methods, filling the gap in privacy evaluation in this domain.
